findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) depicts 5 transformer pads with specific locations and underground electric routing to all 8 buildings. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1 transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' - a single representative symbol without depicting all 5 transformers. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show any transformer pad locations. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) does not show any transformer pad locations. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show any transformer pad locations. The Wet Utilities Plan (Sheet 19) has a legend including transformer symbols but contains no actual electrical infrastructure. Therefore, transformer locations are NOT shown consistently or completely on all required plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires transformer locations shown on site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading/storm plans when applicable. This site has 39 units served by 5 transformers, which should be visible on all plan sheets. Sheet 21 provides detailed electrical information with 5 transformers, but the required discipline plans (landscape, grading, storm) are completely missing this critical infrastructure. Sheet 9 shows only a typical example, not the actual site layout with all 5 transformers. The absence of transformers on landscape and grading plans means Austin Energy and the City cannot verify clearances, access, or conflicts on those plans.
findings.comment: Transformer pad locations must be shown on all plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, grading plan, and storm plan when applicable). Currently, transformers are detailed only on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan), with one typical example on Sheet 9 (Site Plan). Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11), and Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12) do not show any transformer locations. Revise all affected sheets to depict the five transformer pad locations with consistent positioning and labeling.

findings.observation: The site plan set (39 sheets total) includes sheets 1-39 per the README. The sheet index lists sheets 1-39 but does not clearly identify which sheets are architectural elevation sheets. Based on the sheet descriptions, no clearly identified elevation sheets show transformer locations. Sheet 38 is 'Wall Plan' with details and cross-sections, and Sheets 29-37 are addressing, tree, landscape, and canopy/root zone exhibits, but architectural elevation sheets showing transformer locations are not apparent from the available sheet titles.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires transformer locations shown on elevation sheets to verify vertical clearances and building feature conflicts (windows, stairs, doors). This site has 8 buildings with multiple stories (up to 3 stories per Sheet 9 data). Without identified architectural elevation sheets in the plan set, it cannot be determined whether transformers are shown at the required elevations. This could be a missing document type or a labeling issue in the sheet index.
findings.comment: Architectural elevation sheets showing transformer locations are not identified in the plan set. Either provide elevation sheets clearly depicting transformer locations, or clarify whether such sheets are included in the 39-sheet set.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 5 transformer pads with specific locations: northwest (west of Bldg. 1), west-central (west of Bldg. 2), southwest (south of Bldg. 8), east-central (between Bldg. 4 and 5), and southeast (south of Bldg. 6). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1 transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' on the west side south of the main driveway, located between the driveway and Building 8 near a tree well. The single transformer on Sheet 9 is labeled as typical (representative), not showing the actual locations of all 5 transformers required to serve the 8 buildings and 39 units.
findings.reasoning: Transformer locations must be consistent across all plan sheets to enable verification of clearances, conflicts, and infrastructure coordination. Sheet 9 and Sheet 21 show different numbers of transformers and different levels of detail. Sheet 9 appears to show only an example of what a transformer pad symbol looks like, not the actual site-specific locations. This inconsistency creates confusion about which transformers are actually proposed and prevents comprehensive review of clearances and conflicts on the site plan.
findings.comment: Transformer locations shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) are not consistent with Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). Sheet 9 shows one typical example while Sheet 21 shows 5 specific transformer locations. Revise Sheet 9 to show all 5 transformer locations in their actual positions on the site.

findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show transformer pad locations. The vision analysis confirms zero transformers are depicted on the landscape plan. The landscape plan shows building footprints, parking areas, utility lines (labeled as W, SD, OHE), contour lines with elevation labels, trees and vegetation symbols, and landscaping areas with key notes (H.1 through H.7) for paving, street yards, parking lot landscaping, and open space, but no transformers are marked or labeled. The overhead electric line (OHE) is shown on the plan, but transformer locations are not correlated with tree clearance zones.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 restricts tree planting within 10 lateral feet of any side of pad-mounted electric equipment and requires verification on landscape plans. The landscape plan is the discipline responsible for coordinating tree and planting placement with utility infrastructure. Without transformer locations shown on the landscape plan, there is no way to verify that trees are not being planted within the 10-foot clearance zone around any of the 5 transformers. This is a critical safety and compliance issue.
findings.comment: Transformer routing and locations must be shown on the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) to verify tree clearances. Currently, the landscape plan shows no transformer pad locations. Mark all 5 transformer pads on the landscape plan and indicate the 10-foot lateral clearance zones around each pad to ensure trees and plantings do not violate clearance requirements.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads marked as blue squares with leader lines and text labels 'Electrical Transformer Pad' and locations west of Bldg. 1, west of Bldg. 2, south of Bldg. 8, between Bldg. 4-5, and south of Bldg. 6. However, no clearance dimensions are annotated on the plan. No measurements are shown indicating distances from transformer pad edges to: adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, fire escapes, windows, doors, ventilation ducts, or other structures. Sheet 9 shows only one transformer marked as 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' with no clearance dimensions indicated. The vision analysis confirmed that 'There are **no specific measurements, depths, or clearances** shown at the crossing points or along the routing paths on this plan view.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies detailed clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers including: 10 ft clearance to open area, 15 ft to confined spaces, 5 ft from removable fences, 3 ft from certain fence types, 20 ft from fire escapes, 5-12 ft from buildings depending on construction type, and no covering allowed above. Plans must show these clearances are met. Without dimensions and clearance annotations, it is impossible to verify compliance with these requirements. The plans do not demonstrate that clearances are adequate.
findings.comment: Transformer clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 are not shown on the plans. Annotate all transformer pad locations with minimum clearance dimensions showing: distance to nearest building, distance to parking/traffic areas, distance to fire escapes/stairs, distance to windows/doors/vents (if applicable), and verification that no structures overhang the pads. Use dimension lines and callouts to clearly demonstrate compliance with all applicable clearance requirements.

findings.observation: The site plan set includes 39 sheets, but architectural elevation sheets are not clearly identified in the sheet index. Sheets 29 (Addressing Plan), 30 (Existing Tree Plan), 31 (Landscape Plan), 32-37 (Tree/Canopy/Root Zone exhibits), and 38-39 (Wall Plans with details) are described. None of these are identified as architectural elevation sheets showing transformer locations relative to building features (windows, stairs, doors). Without confirmed architectural sheets in the plan set, it cannot be determined if clearances from building features are demonstrated.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires demonstrating clearances from building features on architectural sheets. The visible plan sheets do not include traditional architectural elevations. This could mean: (1) architectural sheets are missing from the plan set, (2) sheets are mislabeled in the index, or (3) architectural design is shown elsewhere. Without architectural elevation sheets clearly showing transformer locations and demonstrating clearances from windows, stairs, doors, and ventilating ducts, this requirement cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Architectural elevation sheets showing transformer clearances from windows, stairs, doors, and ventilating ducts are not identified in the available plan set. Provide architectural elevation views clearly showing all transformer pad locations and dimensions demonstrating minimum clearances per UCM § 1.10.4.

findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has a legend that includes electrical symbols but contains zero actual electrical infrastructure depicted on the plan. Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows only a water tap connection profile to the public right-of-way, with no electrical profile. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 contains no electrical routing or transformer details. Vision analysis confirmed: 'No profile (cross-sectional) views on this sheet' and 'zero electrical infrastructure is drawn on this specific sheet' for Sheet 19.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires plan and profile exhibits showing proximity to existing electrical facilities. This is essential to identify potential conflicts between new transformer/electrical routing and existing utilities. Sheet 21 contains a reference directing to Sheet 19 for profile information, but Sheet 19 does not provide electrical profiles. No plan and profile exhibits are provided showing how the proposed electrical infrastructure relates to existing facilities or how it crosses other utilities.
findings.comment: Plan and profile exhibits showing proximity to existing electrical facilities and how transformer routing/underground electric lines cross other utilities are not provided. Create profile views on the Utility Tap Plan or a separate electrical profile sheet showing: (1) how underground electric lines cross stormwater, wastewater, and water utilities; (2) elevations and depths of electrical routing; (3) clearances from existing utilities.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pad locations with underground electric line routing but does not show: (1) overhead electric lines or existing overhead lines in the vicinity; (2) distances from transformer pads to any existing or proposed overhead lines; (3) any callout or note identifying relationships to existing overhead transmission or distribution lines that may cross the property. The site plan notes reference overhead electric lines (OHE) in the right-of-way along the southern and eastern boundaries, but no specific distance measurements or clearance information is provided relative to transformer locations.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pads must maintain adequate clearances from overhead lines during installation and operation. UCM § 1.16.0 requires showing transformer pad locations and distance from existing overhead lines to ensure safe installation and operation. Without these distances clearly marked, installation crews cannot verify clearances are adequate and safety cannot be assured. Existing overhead lines in/near the right-of-way must be explicitly referenced with distances to proposed transformers.
findings.comment: Transformer pad location and distance from existing overhead lines must be shown on the Electrical Design Plan. Identify all existing or proposed overhead electric lines (including those in Valley View Road right-of-way and on adjacent properties), and annotate distances from each transformer pad to the nearest overhead line. Ensure compliance with applicable clearance requirements.

findings.observation: The site plan shows electric easements labeled with dimensions (5' Electric Easement, 5' Elec. & Tele. Easement) and indicates easements are not within transmission easement areas based on the labeled easement types (distribution easements, not transmission). The facts.md mentions 'No Regulating Plan' applies and the site is not in a Network Area, so transmission easements are not anticipated. Transformer pads are shown on Sheet 21 but not on Sheets 9, 11, 31, or 12, making it impossible to verify whether transformers are within 6 feet of drivable surfaces or if laydown curbs are required. Curbing on the site appears to be standard curb as shown in landscape and grading plans, not laydown curb.
findings.reasoning: Laydown curbs are required only when: (1) curbing is within transmission easement/ROW, OR (2) along Austin Energy truck access routes to transformer pads NOT within 6 feet of drivable surface. The applicability of this item depends on: (A) whether a transmission easement exists on-site (appears not to), and (B) whether any transformer pads are >6 feet from drivable surfaces (cannot be verified from available plans). Without transformer locations on the site plan and landscape plan, distances to drivable surfaces cannot be measured. No indication is given that transformers are in transmission easement areas.
findings.comment: Cannot verify whether laydown curbs are required without transformer locations shown on site plan and landscape plan. If transformers are located >6 feet from parking/traffic areas, identify the required access routes and verify curbing is laydown curb per UCM § 1.14.4 rather than standard curb. This item is conditional on transformer locations being visible on discipline plans.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 pad-mounted transformers and underground electric routing, but shows no drivable access route explicitly marked or labeled. The site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) do not show transformer pad locations at all, making it impossible to verify access routes on those sheets. UCM § 1.10.4 requires that transformer pads be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for Austin Energy truck accessibility, which implies access routes must be shown. The electrical plan shows underground lines routing to transformers but does not indicate drivable access routes or directions for truck access.
findings.reasoning: Drivable access routes to transformer pads are critical for Austin Energy operations (truck must be able to maneuver to pull off a transformer for replacement/repair). Without visible access routes shown on the plans, it cannot be verified that adequate access is provided. The standard is that pads should be within 6 feet of drivable parking/traffic surfaces. If a pad is further away, a dedicated access route must be shown. Without access routes clearly indicated on the site and landscape plans, this requirement cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Drivable access routes to all transformer pads must be shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Use arrows, dashed lines, or other clear notation to identify how Austin Energy trucks can access each transformer pad. Ensure each pad is located within 6 feet of a drivable surface (parking or traffic area) per UCM § 1.10.4, or provide marked dedicated access routes.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 explicitly references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' in a callout directing readers to Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) for profile information on transformer routing. However, vision analysis of Sheet 19 confirmed: 'No profile (cross-sectional) views on this sheet. The entire drawing is a single plan (top-down) view.' Additionally, 'zero electrical infrastructure is drawn on this specific sheet' - the legend includes electrical symbols but they are not used in the actual plan. Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) contains only water line profiles, not electrical. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows storm drainage system but no electrical routing crossing information.
findings.reasoning: When electrical routing crosses stormwater piping, a profile or cross-section must show the vertical relationship, depths, and clearances. Sheet 21 directs readers to Sheet 19 for this profile, but Sheet 19 contains no electrical information whatsoever. This is a critical coordination gap - without profiles showing how electrical routing crosses storm drain lines, depth conflicts cannot be identified and safe installation cannot be ensured.
findings.comment: Profile showing how transformer routing and underground electric lines cross stormwater piping is not provided. Sheet 21 references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 contains no electrical infrastructure. Provide cross-sectional profile(s) showing: (1) the vertical alignment of underground electric lines at points where they cross storm drain pipes; (2) depths of each utility; (3) clearances between utilities; (4) any separations or protection required for safe co-location.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads marked with blue square symbols and labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad' at their locations, but no transformer door locations are indicated. No callouts, arrows, or detailed insets show which side of each pad contains the door opening, the direction the door swings, the clearance needed for door operation, or any operating access information. The vision analysis noted that transformers are marked only with their general location but no specific door information is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires clear indication of transformer door locations because: (1) door location determines which side requires operating clearance, (2) door location affects required clearance dimensions (different clearances for different sides per § 1.10.4), and (3) door location must be known to verify sufficient space for door swing and equipment access. Without this information, clearances cannot be properly verified.
findings.comment: Transformer door location must be clearly indicated for each of the five pad-mounted transformers on Sheet 21. Use arrows, labels, or detailed callouts to show the side of each pad where the operating door is located, and indicate the direction of door swing. This is necessary to verify that clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 are adequate for equipment access.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows electrical easements labeled with recording information (Vol. numbers, Pg numbers, document references) such as '5' Electric & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' However, these labeled easements are plat-dedicated easements of record (existing easements), not proposed easements around the transformer facilities. The facts.md lists several existing electric easements (5' electric easements per plat documents) but no analysis is provided showing whether these existing easements are adequate to cover the 5 transformer pad locations, their required clearances (which can range from 3-15 feet per UCM § 1.10.4), and access requirements. No proposed electrical easement is shown around transformer facilities.
findings.reasoning: Electrical easements around transformer facilities must be shown or proposed with adequate dimensions to cover physical location, all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4, and access requirements per UCM § 1.3.24. Existing plat-dedicated easements shown on Sheet 21 are 5 feet wide, but transformer clearance requirements can extend 10-15 feet depending on equipment orientation and building features. Unless a detailed analysis demonstrates existing easements are sufficient, proposed easement dedications or modifications must be shown.
findings.comment: Electrical easement dimensions must be adequate to cover transformer facilities and required clearances. Analyze whether existing 5-foot electric easements shown on the plat are sufficient for the five transformer pads, or propose new/modified easements. Show all easement boundaries clearly on Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) with dimensions and recording information. Easement widths must accommodate the transformer pad physical location plus all clearance requirements (up to 15 feet depending on location and equipment orientation).

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads marked with blue square symbols and labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' at their locations (NW, W-central, SW, E-central, SE). While the transformers are labeled with the equipment type 'Electrical Transformer Pad,' they are not individually labeled with unique identifiers (e.g., 'XFMR-1', 'XFMR-2', etc.) that would allow specific reference in specifications, electrical calculations, or coordination with other disciplines. This generic labeling without individual identification creates ambiguity in referring to specific transformers.
findings.reasoning: Clear identification and labeling of each transformer is essential for permit review, coordination with other trades, and construction. Generic labels like 'Electrical Transformer Pad' do not distinguish between the five different transformers. Each transformer should be uniquely labeled so that specifications, clearance calculations, meter assignments, and building connections can be clearly correlated to specific equipment. This is standard engineering practice for electrical documentation.
findings.comment: Individual transformer labels are missing on the plans. Assign unique identifiers to each of the five transformer pads (e.g., 'XFMR-1', 'XFMR-2', 'XFMR-3', 'XFMR-4', 'XFMR-5') and show these labels clearly on Sheet 21 and on all other plan sheets where transformers appear. This will enable clear cross-referencing in specifications and coordination documents.

findings.observation: The 5 transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 are labeled only as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no size specification. No callouts, notes, or specifications indicate the kVA capacity of any transformer. No table or legend provides transformer specifications. The vision analysis confirmed: 'Size/Capacity: Not specified' for all five transformers. Without size information, it cannot be verified that transformer capacity is adequate to serve the development's electrical demand.
findings.reasoning: Transformer size (kVA rating) is essential information for: (1) verifying adequate capacity to serve all buildings, (2) determining construction, operation, and maintenance needs, (3) establishing clearance requirements, and (4) coordinating with Austin Energy. UCM § 1.16.0 requires complete and detailed electrical facility information. Omitting transformer sizes is a significant deficiency.
findings.comment: Transformer size (kVA) must be specified for each of the five transformer pads on Sheet 21. Include a specification note, callout label, or table showing: (1) transformer kVA rating for each pad, (2) quantity (number of units at each location), (3) metering method, and (4) buildings served by each transformer.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pad locations marked with blue square symbols. No dimension callouts are provided on Sheet 21 for the pad dimensions themselves (length and width of the equipment pad). Vision analysis stated: 'Transformer pad dimensions not consistent across all plan sheets.' Since transformers are not shown on Sheets 9, 11, 31, or 12, pad dimensions cannot be verified on any sheet other than Sheet 21. On Sheet 21, no specific pad dimension measurements (e.g., 24" × 36", 30" × 48") are annotated.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pad dimensions (length and width) must be shown on all plan sheets where transformers appear to ensure consistency and allow verification of clearances and access. Sheet 21 shows transformer locations but no pad dimensions are annotated. Since transformers don't appear on other sheets, consistency across sheets cannot be evaluated. Standard pad-mounted transformer dimensions should be specified in the electrical specifications or on the plans.
findings.comment: Transformer pad dimensions must be shown on all plan sheets depicting transformers. Provide specific dimensions for each pad (length × width) on Sheet 21 and verify the same dimensions are shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Grading Plan (Sheet 11) where transformers are added. Typical pad-mounted transformer pads are often 24" × 36" or 30" × 48" - specify the exact size for this project.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads serving 8 buildings with 39 units total. The buildings are described as 4-plexes, 5-plexes, and 6-plexes with gross floor areas ranging from 3,290 sf to 4,997 sf per building. The electrical plan shows 5 transformers but provides no specification indicating: (1) the total capacity of all transformers combined, (2) the electrical demand of all 39 units and 8 buildings, (3) the load distribution among the 5 transformers, or (4) whether the total transformer capacity is adequate to serve all buildings. No transformer sizing analysis or electrical load calculation is provided.
findings.reasoning: Transformer capacity must be adequate to serve all buildings in the development. This is a fundamental design requirement. Without showing transformer sizes and confirming that total capacity meets or exceeds the calculated electrical demand for 39 residential units, the adequacy of the electrical service cannot be verified. Austin Energy design review typically requires load calculations demonstrating adequate capacity.
findings.comment: Confirm that transformer capacity is adequate to serve all 39 units and 8 buildings. Provide electrical load calculations showing: (1) total electrical demand for the development, (2) the kVA rating of each of the 5 transformers, (3) the total combined capacity, and (4) confirmation that capacity exceeds demand with appropriate safety margin. Show this information on Sheet 21 in a specifications table or notes section.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' and 8 meters labeled as 'Electrical Meters' but does not provide metering method designations for any transformer. No notes or callouts indicate whether the transformers are: (1) CT metered (current transformer metered at transformer, with meters located remotely at buildings), or (2) building metered (meters located at each customer/building adjacent to transformer). The vision analysis confirmed: 'Metering Method: Not labeled' for all five transformers.
findings.reasoning: The metering method (CT metered vs. building metered) is critical information that determines: (1) where meters are located, (2) where service disconnects must be positioned, (3) clearance and access requirements, and (4) coordination between transformer location and meter location. UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be within sight of the transformer. The metering method must be clearly specified on plans so that meter locations can be verified as compliant.
findings.comment: Metering method must be labeled for each transformer on Sheet 21. Specify whether each transformer is: (1) CT metered (with meters located at individual buildings), or (2) building metered (with grouped meters at central location). This designation must correlate with meter locations shown on the plans and must confirm that meters remain within sight of transformers per UCM § 1.9.3.1.B.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) does not include a title block legend or notation delineating transformers, meters, and pull boxes as proposed utilities. The plan has leader lines pointing to individual equipment with text labels ('Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Meters', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Underground Electric Line') but no formal legend or symbol key is shown on the sheet. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) mentions overhead electric lines but shows limited electrical symbols. No formal legend on either sheet identifies proposed electrical utilities with symbols and explains what each symbol represents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that proposed utilities be clearly delineated in plan legends. A proper legend helps readers understand the plan symbols and ensures consistency across all sheets. Without a legend on the electrical plans identifying transformers, meters, pull boxes, and underground lines as proposed utilities, the plans are incomplete. Other disciplines reviewing the electrical plans must have clear symbol definitions.
findings.comment: Add a legend to Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identifying all proposed electrical utilities with symbols and descriptions, including: Transformer Pad, Electrical Meter, Pull Box, Underground Electric Line, and any other electrical facilities shown. Also add or enhance the legend on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to clearly show proposed electrical infrastructure symbols. Ensure symbols are consistent with any legend shown on other utility plan sheets (Sheets 19, 20).

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations labeled as 'Electrical Meters' positioned on or near each of the 8 buildings (Bldg. 1-8). However: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show meter locations - no meters are labeled or visible; (2) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show meter locations - vision analysis confirmed 'No meter locations are shown or labeled'; (3) Sheet 19 (Wet Utilities Plan) contains a legend that includes symbols for meters but no actual meter locations are depicted on the plan drawing. Therefore, meter locations are NOT shown on all required plan sheets as specified in the checklist.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.A requires meter locations shown on site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. This allows review of meter accessibility, visibility to transformer, and clearance from other utilities and building features. Sheet 21 shows meters but they must also be shown on the Site Plan, Wet Utilities Plan, and Landscape Plan for complete coordination.
findings.comment: Meter locations must be shown on all required plan sheets. Add 8 meter locations to: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan) - mark meter positions on each building; (2) Sheet 19 or 20 (Wet Utilities Plan) - show meter positions relative to water, wastewater, and storm drain utilities; (3) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) - show meter positions to verify clearances from plantings. Label all meters with unique identifiers matching the electrical plan.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters labeled generically as 'Electrical Meters' and 8 pull boxes labeled as 'Electrical Pull Box' without individual identifiers. No unique labels (e.g., 'METER-1', 'METER-2', 'PB-1', 'PB-2', etc.) are provided. While the meters and pull boxes are positioned on the plan, they cannot be specifically referenced or correlated with building designations without individual identification. No specification table or notes section provides meter and disconnect information.
findings.reasoning: Each meter and disconnect must be individually labeled and identified so that: (1) it can be specifically referenced in specifications and coordination documents, (2) building service connections can be clearly traced, (3) service upgrades can be implemented with precision, and (4) inspectors can verify the correct equipment is installed. Generic labels are inadequate.
findings.comment: Individual labels are required for all meters and disconnects. Assign unique identifiers to each of the 8 meters (e.g., 'M-1' through 'M-8' corresponding to Buildings 1-8) and to all pull boxes (e.g., 'PB-1', 'PB-2', etc.). Show these labels clearly on Sheet 21 and on all other plan sheets where meters appear. Create a meter schedule or specification table on the electrical plan showing meter identification, building served, location, and type.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations and 5 transformer locations. The vision analysis indicated that meters are 'generally corresponding to the eight buildings on the site' and transformers are distributed across the site with underground electric routing connecting them. However, no explicit visual confirmation is shown on the plan that each meter has clear line-of-sight visibility to its serving transformer. No callouts, sight-line diagrams, or notes state that meters are within sight of transformers. The arrangement suggests meters should be visible to transformers (given underground routing), but this critical requirement is not explicitly documented on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be 'within sight of an Austin Energy transformer.' This is a specific requirement for safety and operations. Without explicit sight-line confirmation on the plans, or without a note stating that meters are positioned for visibility, there is no documented verification of compliance. Additionally, the plans do not state whether any exceptions requiring AE Design approval are being claimed.
findings.comment: Verify and document that all meter locations are within sight of serving transformers per UCM § 1.9.3.1.B. Add a note to Sheet 21 stating: 'All meters are located within sight of their serving transformer. No line-of-sight exceptions are claimed.' OR, if any meter locations do not have clear sight-line visibility, provide documentation of written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering for the exception. Alternatively, add sight-line symbols or dashed lines from each meter to its serving transformer to visually demonstrate visibility.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters and pull boxes but does not explicitly identify which location is the point-of-service (point where AE conductors connect to customer conductors). The grouping definition states that Point-of-Service is the 'meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or AE-approved enclosure where AE and Customer conductors connect.' Without a clear label or callout indicating the point-of-service location, it cannot be determined where Austin Energy's responsibility ends and customer responsibility begins.
findings.reasoning: The point-of-service is the critical junction where utility responsibility transfers from Austin Energy to the customer. It must be clearly marked on plans so that: (1) Austin Energy and customer can verify the boundary of responsibility, (2) disconnects are properly located, (3) permits can be accurately issued, and (4) inspections can verify correct installation. Without explicit identification, there is ambiguity about which equipment serves this critical function.
findings.comment: Clearly identify the point-of-service location on Sheet 21. Label the specific equipment (meter socket, service distribution enclosure, pull box, or other approved enclosure) that serves as the point where Austin Energy facilities connect to customer conductors. Add a note stating the point-of-service definition and location(s). This should be shown for each service/building connection.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 pull boxes labeled as 'Electrical Pull Box' positioned throughout the site on the underground electric routing. However, the vision analysis determined that these are likely pull boxes for the electrical service routing (standard for underground utility systems) but the plans do not explicitly state whether pull boxes are 'required by electrical service design' or whether they are only being provided as standard practice. The distinction matters for this checklist item: if pull boxes are required per Austin Energy design specifications, then showing them is required; if they're optional, then omitting them would not be a deficiency.
findings.reasoning: The applicability note for EL-15.37 states 'Only when pull boxes required by electrical service design.' This checklist item is conditional. Pull boxes are standard in underground electrical systems for drawing cable and navigation, but they must be explicitly required by Austin Energy or electrical specifications to trigger this checklist requirement. Without clear indication that pull boxes are required by design, the applicability cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: If pull boxes are required by Austin Energy electrical service design specifications, confirm their locations are shown on all utility plan sheets. If not required, this item is not applicable. Clarify in the electrical specifications whether pull boxes are required or optional for this installation.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads and 8 pull boxes but does not show any load center location. The applicability note states this item is only required 'when load centers required by project electrical design.' No load center is indicated on the preliminary electrical plan shown. It is not clear from the submitted plans whether a load center is required for this project or whether the building service connections are made directly from meters.
findings.reasoning: Load centers are not always required; they depend on the electrical service design and building layout. The applicability of this item depends on whether the project's electrical design includes a centralized load center. Without an explicit requirement stated in the electrical design documents or specifications, this item's applicability cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: If a load center is required by the project electrical design, show its location on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). If no load center is required, note in the electrical specifications that the design uses distributed building-level service without a central load center. Clarify this in the design submittal.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' but does not explicitly show any separate manhole locations distinct from pull boxes. Pull boxes and manholes are different - pull boxes are small access points for drawing cable, while manholes are larger access points for vault-like underground utility infrastructure (such as underground transformer vaults or junction points). The plans do not indicate whether any true underground vaults or transformer vaults are required. The applicability note states 'Only when manholes required for electrical service,' which is a conditional applicability requirement.
findings.reasoning: Manhole locations are only relevant if the electrical service design includes underground vaults, transformer vaults, or other vault-like installations. The current design shows pad-mounted surface transformers and pull boxes, not underground vaults. Without explicit indication that underground vaults requiring manhole access are part of the design, this item may not be applicable.
findings.comment: Clarify whether this project includes any underground electrical vaults or transformer vaults requiring manhole access. If only pull boxes are used (as currently shown), this item is not applicable. If underground vaults are required, show manhole locations on all required plan sheets (site, wet utilities, landscape).

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads but does not display bollard symbols or callouts. The checklist item specifically applies 'only when pad-mounted transformer is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas.' Transformers are not shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or other discipline plans, making it impossible to accurately measure distances from transformer pads to the nearest parking or traffic areas using the plans. Sheet 21 shows the site layout and parking areas, but without clear transformer locations and precise measurements marked, the 4-foot threshold cannot be verified from available evidence.
findings.reasoning: This item is conditionally applicable only if any of the 5 transformers are located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. While Sheet 21 shows both transformers and parking areas, the distance relationship is not explicitly annotated with dimensions. To verify whether bollards are required, the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area must be measured or explicitly noted on the plans. Without such measurements, the applicability cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: Measure the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area on Sheet 21. If any transformer is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas, show bollard locations and spacing (sized to allow equipment door opening) on the Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Site Plan (Sheet 9), and Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). If all transformers are more than 4 feet from parking/traffic areas, note this on the plan.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 pad-mounted transformers but does not indicate whether they are oil-filled (which requires drainage considerations) or dry-type. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show transformer pad locations, so there are no grading details or drainage arrows visible around any transformer pads. No contour lines, spot elevations, or drainage flow arrows are shown in the vicinity of transformer locations. If the transformers are oil-filled, UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 1 requires grading to direct liquid flow away from buildings.
findings.reasoning: Oil-filled transformers pose an environmental and safety risk if oil leaks. Grading must be designed to prevent spilled oil from flowing toward buildings. This requirement only applies to oil-filled transformers. Without: (1) specification of whether transformers are oil-filled or dry-type, and (2) grading details around oil-filled transformers (if applicable), compliance cannot be verified. The omission of transformer locations from the Grading Plan means this critical drainage requirement cannot be addressed.
findings.comment: Specify whether transformers are oil-filled or dry-type on the Electrical Design Plan. If oil-filled: (1) Show transformer pad locations on Grading Plan (Sheet 11) with contour lines and spot elevations; (2) Add drainage arrows or notes confirming that ground grading slopes away from transformer pads and toward properties; (3) Verify that no oil spill pathway leads toward building foundations or sensitive areas.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads and the site plan shows no fuel storage, chemical storage, flammable liquids facilities, or hazardous material storage areas. The site is a residential townhome development with water service, wastewater service, and stormwater facilities. No indication is given that flammable liquids are stored or handled on-site.
findings.reasoning: This checklist item is conditional: 'Only when flammable liquid storage or handling occurs on site.' Without evidence that flammable liquids are present on-site, this item may not be applicable. The site appears to be residential only without commercial operations involving hazardous materials.
findings.comment: Confirm whether flammable liquid storage or handling occurs on this site. If no flammable liquids are stored or handled, this item is not applicable. If flammable liquid storage is planned, provide documentation of AE Design approval for transformer location relative to flammable liquid facilities.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations labeled as 'Electrical Meters' but does not provide specific callouts showing distances from each meter to gas meters, regulators, relief valves, or other electrical apparatus. The site plan does not show gas meter locations or other utility equipment that might create conflicts. Without detailed site analysis showing the location of all meters and utility apparatus, the 3-foot separation requirement cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: This requirement depends on identifying all gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus on the site, then verifying at least 3-foot separation from electrical meters. Sheet 21 does not provide this level of detail for meter-to-utility spacing.
findings.comment: Verify that all electrical meter locations maintain minimum 3-foot separation from gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus per UCM § 1.9.3.1.C. If gas appliances or other utility apparatus are present, show their locations on the Electrical Design Plan and annotate distances to electrical meters.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations and transformer locations, but does not specify which meters are paired with which disconnects, nor does it provide distance callouts showing meter-to-disconnect distances. The checklist item requires: (1) meter to disconnect distance not to exceed 20 feet, and (2) meter and disconnect within line of sight. Without explicit labeling of meter-disconnect pairs and distance callouts, these requirements cannot be verified from the plans.
findings.reasoning: This requirement is conditional on having grouped metering with associated disconnects. If meters and disconnects are paired, their locations and distances must be clearly shown and verified on the plans. Sheet 21 does not provide sufficient detail for this verification.
findings.comment: If meters and disconnects are paired, show their spatial relationship on Sheet 21 with: (1) clear identification of meter-disconnect pairs, (2) distance callouts showing the separation between each meter and its disconnect, (3) verification that distance does not exceed 20 feet, and (4) confirmation that meters and disconnects are within line of sight of each other. If meters and disconnects are not paired, clarify the electrical service configuration.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 pad-mounted transformer pads, all positioned outside buildings on the site surface. There is no indication of any niche service (specialized transformer installation within building footprint, accessible from exterior). The applicability note states this item applies 'only when transformer service via specialized niche' and requires 'transformer service via specialized niche (equipment within building footprint, accessible from exterior, site outside Network Area).' The site plan shows all transformers as surface pad-mounted equipment, not niches.
findings.reasoning: Niche service is a specialized configuration where transformer equipment is installed within a building's footprint but remains accessible from the exterior for Austin Energy access. This is fundamentally different from the pad-mounted transformers shown on the plans. Without indication of niche service in the design, this item does not apply.
findings.comment: If niche service is required or proposed for any transformer, provide: (1) niche plan showing equipment location within building footprint, (2) profile showing niche dimensions and exterior access, (3) evidence of AE Design consultation and approval. If only pad-mounted transformers are used (as currently shown), this item is not applicable.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows a single development with 8 buildings and 39 units served by 5 transformers. The applicability note states: 'Only for multi-site developments. Check: project description or site plan for number of distinct sites.' The site plan (Sheet 9) describes the project as a single site: 'Valley View Townhomes' on 'Lot 1, Mecey Subdivision.' The facts.md confirms a single parcel (Parcel ID 0406100252, 2.16 acres). There is no indication this is a multi-site development.
findings.reasoning: This item is conditional on the project being a multi-site development where each site should have its own transformer. The Valley View Townhomes project is a single development on a single lot. Therefore, this item does not apply.
findings.comment: If this is a multi-site development (multiple distinct sites, each potentially serving independent customer groups), verify that each site has its own transformer. If this is a single-site development (as currently described), this item is not applicable.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads serving 8 buildings. The applicability note states: 'Only when two or more transformers proposed or otherwise required per Austin Energy Design. Check: transformer count on plans or Austin Energy requirements letter.' Five transformers are proposed, which appears to meet the threshold of 'two or more.' However, the note also requires 'AE Design coordination to determine applicability' for switchgear location. No switchgear location is shown on the plans, and no documentation indicates whether Austin Energy Design has specified a switchgear requirement for this configuration.
findings.reasoning: Switchgear may or may not be required depending on Austin Energy's specific design for this project. The plans do not indicate whether switchgear is part of the approved electrical design. Without explicit Austin Energy Design coordination documentation, the applicability of this switchgear requirement cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: If Austin Energy Design requires switchgear for this multi-transformer configuration, show the switchgear location on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). Provide documentation of Austin Energy coordination confirming whether switchgear is required. If switchgear is not required, note this in the electrical specifications.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters labeled as 'Electrical Meters' positioned individually on or near each building (Bldg. 1-8). The applicability note states: 'Only when two or more meters are installed at one location and served from one set of service conductors. Check: electrical plan for number of meters and service configuration.' The current design shows 8 separate meter locations, one per building, not multiple meters at a single location served from one service point. There is no meter bank or grouped meter installation shown.
findings.reasoning: This item applies to meter bank/rack configurations where multiple meters are physically located together at one point of service. The current design shows distributed metering with individual meters at each building. Therefore, this item does not apply.
findings.comment: If the electrical design includes any grouped meter configuration (two or more meters at a single location served from one service point), show the meter bank/rack location on Sheet 21. If meters are distributed individually to each building (as currently shown), this item is not applicable.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 does not show any existing meter locations. The applicability note states: 'Only when existing meters present on site. Check: utility locate documentation or survey for existing meters.' The site plan indicates this is vacant land following demolition of a prior assisted living facility (demolished June 2022 per facts.md). The survey and plan submissions do not indicate existing electrical meters on the current site. Therefore, no existing meter locations require documentation.
findings.reasoning: This item applies only if existing meters are currently on the site. For a development on a vacant site (demolished and cleared), there would be no existing meters to show.
findings.comment: If any existing electrical meters remain on the site from prior development, show their locations on the plans. If the site is vacant and cleared (as indicated), this item is not applicable.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters distributed individually to 8 buildings (one meter per building) and 5 transformers distributed across the site. The applicability note states: 'Only when multiple meters are served from one set of service conductors or when meters and disconnects must be grouped per code. Check: electrical service configuration showing single point of service serving multiple units.' The current design shows 8 separate service connections (one per building), not multiple meters served from a single service point.
findings.reasoning: This requirement applies to grouped metering configurations where multiple meter units share a common service point. The current electrical design shows individual building-level service, not grouped multi-unit metering. Therefore, this item does not apply.
findings.comment: If the electrical design includes grouped metering for multiple buildings from a single service point, verify that meters and disconnects are grouped in a common location with service distribution enclosure and wireway per UCM § 1.9.3.4. If individual building service is provided (as currently shown), this item is not applicable.

findings.observation: The facts.md confirms the site is in 'FEMA Flood Zone: Zone X (outside 100-year and 500-year floodplain)' and 'COA Flood Zone: Zone X' with 'Floodplain intersection: None.' Sheet 21 does not indicate meter elevations relative to flood levels because the site is not subject to the 100-Year Reference Flood Datum requirement. The applicability note states: 'Only when site is subject to 100-Year Reference Flood Datum ordinance.' Since the site is in Zone X (no floodplain), this requirement does not apply.
findings.reasoning: This item applies only to sites within a 100-year floodplain subject to elevation requirements. The Valley View Townhomes site is outside the floodplain in Zone X, so flood elevation requirements do not apply.
findings.comment: Since the site is in FEMA Flood Zone X (outside 100-year floodplain), minimum flood elevation requirements for meters do not apply. This item is not applicable.

findings.reasoning: This item applies only if existing pull boxes are present from prior development. For a vacant, cleared site, there would be no existing pull boxes to show.
findings.comment: If any existing electrical pull boxes or utility infrastructure remain from prior development, show their locations on the plans. If the site is vacant and cleared, this item is not applicable.

findings.comment: If any existing electrical vaults or manholes remain from prior development, show their locations on the plans. If the site is vacant and cleared (as indicated), this item is not applicable.

findings.observation: The applicability note states: 'Only when pole or driveway relocation required. Check: survey for existing poles/driveways in conflict with proposed development.'
